news.title: PGA Division 1 report: Chelsea Women Under-18s 10-2 Birmingham City
news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s, who play in Division 1 of the PGA Women’s Under-21 League, produced a dominant display at Kingsmeadow on Sunday, scoring ten goals against Birmingham City. Despite conceding inside the opening minute, the Blues responded impressively, netting three times shortly before the break and then adding seven more goals after the interval. Seven different Chelsea players got on the scoresheet, with the result extending our unbeaten start to the Division 1 campaign. The performance also featured contributions from several members of our Under-16s squad. The visitors made a dream start, scoring just 22 seconds after kick-off. A misplaced pass allowed Birmingham to move forward quickly and, after working the ball into the penalty area, they found the net from close range. Chelsea responded positively and began to establish control of possession, with our pressure rewarded in the 38th minute. Keira Johnson set the ball back for Tess Finn, who drove beyond the Birmingham defence before finishing from inside the penalty area to equalise. Four minutes later, the Blues went ahead. Nelly Las and Johnson combined on the right before the latter's cross was cut out. The clearance fell to Maria Mayers on the edge of the area, and she took a touch before firing into the top-left corner and celebrating in style (top). There was still time for another before the break. Straight from kick-off, Las played the ball forward to Ella Abayomi, whose pass across the edge of the penalty area found Gabi Storey. The defender struck first time, sending an excellent effort beyond the goalkeeper to make it 3-1. Chelsea maintained their attacking momentum in the second half, with Abayomi adding her name to the scoresheet five minutes after the restart. Las delivered from the right and Abayomi finished confidently inside the penalty area. Jahmya Putman made it five in the 61st minute. Chloe Sarwie released Aysia Matabaro down the left, and the winger reached the byline before cutting the ball back for Putman to finish first time. A Birmingham defender then turned Sarwie's inswinging corner into her own net in the 66th minute, before Abayomi scored her second two minutes later. Matabaro again provided the delivery, picking out the forward inside the box for a composed finish. Storey then claimed her second of the afternoon in the 75th minute, meeting Las's pass with a shot that flew past the goalkeeper. Birmingham pulled one back a minute later after a long clearance caused problems for the Chelsea defence, allowing their striker to run through and score. The Blues responded with two more goals. Matabaro drove through the penalty area before finishing with her right foot in the 79th minute, following Maria Mayers' pass. The scoring was completed in the 88th minute. Mayers regained possession and found Matabaro on the left, whose cross reached Las. She controlled before shooting, with a deflection helping the ball find the top corner to complete the 10-goal haul. The victory means Chelsea remain unbeaten in PGA Division 1 after four matches, collecting ten points from a possible 12 as we head into the international break. The Blues now take a break from domestic action, with several members of the squad set to represent their countries at Under-17 and Under-19 level. Chelsea return to PGA Division 1 action on Wednesday 9 December, when we travel to face Bristol City. Chelsea (3-4-3): Victoria Rudz (Bella Bartlett 63); Zoe Ciccardini (Annie Boichat 45), Gabi Storey, Sadie Gregory; Maria Mayers, Tess Finn, Keira Johnson (Ella Abayomi 45), Rebekah Pierce (Chloe Sarwie 45); Nelly Las, Carla Gardiner (Jahmya Putman 45), Aysia MatabaroScorers: Finn 38, Mayers 42, Storey 45, 75, Abayomi 50, 68, Putman 61, Own goal 66, Matabaro 79, Las 88Booked: Boichat 90

news.title: Bompastor: Lola Brown’s mentality is ‘unbelievable’
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor was full of praise for Lola Brown after her impressive Chelsea cameo in our Women’s Super League draw with Liverpool. The 19-year-old came off the bench and had a big impact on the left flank, causing trouble for the hosts and creating a chance for Sjoeke Nusken that forced a fantastic save from Khiara Keating in the Liverpool goal. Bompastor said that while competition for places is currently high, Brown’s mentality has been ‘unbelievable’ as she looks to earn more time on the pitch. ‘Lola didn't get many minutes [previously],’ Bompastor said. ‘The competition is high in this squad with many experienced players. ‘What she's been doing since the summer has been good, really good. Her mentality is unbelievable; she always works hard and puts a big effort on the pitch. ‘The quality she brings with the ball, she's a really confident player. I just felt from what I could observe in this game, she was probably the right profile to come on as the left wing-back. ‘I think we wanted to create more with crosses. She did well, we couldn't convert some of the crosses that she put in the box, but again from everyone I had available on the bench, she was probably the right profile to replace Sandy Baltimore.’ Brown has been called up to England Women’s Under-23s squad for the forthcoming international break, with matches against Belgium and Portugal on the agenda.

news.title: Romeo Lavia: This is not the moment to panic
news.body_en: Romeo Lavia says Chelsea must use the pain of yesterday's 4-1 defeat to Leeds United as fuel to provoke a strong reaction, starting with our trip to Nottingham Forest next week. The Blues started brightly at Stamford Bridge and deservedly took the lead midway through the first half when Emmanuel Emegha marked his full debut with a clinical left-footed finish. However, Noah Okafor levelled just three minutes later, and after Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted from the penalty spot early in the second half, further strikes from Okafor and Brenden Aaronson condemned us to a heavy home defeat. Lavia did not hide his frustration at letting a promising start slip away, though he was clear that the dressing room will remain calm and united. ‘Everyone is very angry and disappointed,’ said Lavia. ‘At home this is never the way you want to finish a game. We let them back in the game when we shouldn’t have. This is something we will analyse and get better at. ‘When we won games, when we lost games, we always said that no matter what, it’s a process,’ Lavia added. ‘With these types of results, it feels like the end of the world, but we are not going to ring the bell now to say it’s a panic moment. Not at all. We are very confident as a team. We know where we want to get to. ‘This hurts, it needs to hurt so it provokes a reaction from the team, and this is definitely going to help us for the next game on Friday.’ Lavia also acknowledged the disappointment felt by supporters inside Stamford Bridge. The Belgian emphasised that the players take full accountability for falling short of the standards expected. ‘Of course, this is Chelsea Football Club, a club that wins trophies and is expected at the highest level every time,’ Lavia said. ‘At home it hurts times ten. You always want to give the fans what they deserve, and that wasn’t the case. We understand it and we take full responsibility.’

news.title: Keeper voted Star of the Match in Liverpool stalemate
news.body_en: Hannah Hampton has been voted the Chelsea Women Star of the Match in our goalless draw with Liverpool. In a closely contested encounter where neither side could find a breakthrough, it was our goalkeeper who stood out most to supporters who gave their verdict in our poll on the Chelsea Official App. Hampton earned 45 per cent of the vote to claim the accolade. The keeper made a couple of important first-half saves to keep the game goalless, and her calm distribution was a key part of our build-up play. Youngster Lola Brown finished second in the poll with 24 per cent after an energetic and fearless performance after coming off the bench, while Ellie Carpenter was third with 17 per cent of the vote following a typically tireless display with contributions at both ends.

news.title: Alonso: We need to be tougher to recover from setbacks
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has identified the key area his Chelsea team needs to improve as he reflects on a disappointing afternoon at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, believing we have to learn to take a 'punch' and bounce back stronger. Despite taking the lead against Leeds United through Emmanuel Emegha’s first goal for the club, the Blues never recovered after the visitors responded with a quick equaliser, as three second-half goals condemned us to a 4-1 defeat in the Premier League. Our manager admitted it was a particularly tough result to take given the rivalry between the two clubs, as he shared the supporters’ frustration at the final whistle. ‘I understand their disappointment for sure, and we share that with them,’ he said. ‘The only thing we can do is work, try to give our best to turn it back and to do much better. ‘We were disappointed, the fans were disappointed. We were disappointed because the expectations from them are high and we feel sorry for them. We need to go through this together and to find solutions together. ‘Now, for sure, it's not the easiest moment. We're in a fragile moment, but we need to work together and stick together, because there’s still such a long way to go.’ In order to find those solutions, Alonso wants his team to be more resilient to bounce back from on-pitch setbacks, an area he feels we lacked both in Saturday’s game and the loss away at Sunderland before the international break. That is along with better handling opponents like those, who take a physical and direct approach to the game, especially given it is something he expects us to face on a regular basis in the Premier League. ‘We need to find solutions for sure, because there will be setbacks during any game, and we have to be tougher and to be able to go through that and to know that there’s still so long to play. It's something mandatory in this competition. ‘I felt that probably we are in a fragile moment mentally, in our confidence. When we received a punch we didn't recover from that strong or tough enough. That was my feeling. ‘We need to deal with that because this is the demand of the Premier League. Not just yesterday. When we go on Friday against Forest, this will happen to them. There were moments that we were not competing at the level required. We need to know that's mandatory in this competition, because we will face teams with that demand again. ‘But the physicality, the duels, that is not the only explanation. We could do better in a football way – not giving the ball away, trying to progress a little bit more, choosing better options. But as well, the physicality and the mentality are parts we can do better. ‘Our job is to try to find solutions, to work on that, to have experiences – bad experiences like yesterday, and hopefully we will have good ones when we can – and overcome even during the game a difficult moment, because this is football and for sure that will happen. In the progression, in the process that I often talk about, this is a very important topic.’ Alonso now has just under a week to work with his team at Cobham to try to rectify those issues before our next fixture, when we travel to Nottingham Forest for the Premier League’s Friday evening kick-off.

news.title: Bronze frustrated after dominant display against Liverpool
news.body_en: Lucy Bronze admitted she and her Chelsea team-mates were frustrated after being unable to convert their dominance over Liverpool into a win in the Women’s Super League. The 0-0 draw on Saturday leaves the Blues two points clear at the top of the table, but Manchester City will be in action on Sunday with a chance to reclaim top spot before the international break. It was a performance full of control for Sonia Bompastor’s side, especially in the second half, but Liverpool keeper Khiara Keating was in inspired form, with a save from Sjoeke Nusken the pick of her numerous saves. After coming away with a point from St Helens Stadium, Bronze said the team have to score more goals from the chances they are creating, a theme that has troubled them at times already this year. ‘Yeah, [it was frustrating],’ Bronze said. ‘Especially after the second half. ‘First half was a bit more even, although we created some good chances, they had one or two as well, Hannah had some good saves - more than she usually has. ‘But then the second half, I think we completely dominated the game. It just felt like Nusken's chance at the end, probably on another day, that goes in the back of the net, and a few other chances as well. Obviously Khiara Keating had a great game.' Bronze acknowledged that Saturday's draw with Liverpool was reflective of several matches already this season and recognised the Blues expect more. She continued: 'The end product was there a few times, but the goalkeeper saved it. We need to create more, we need to do more, score more goals. 'I think that's been the story of our season - not scoring as many goals in certain games as we should do. Thinking of the draws we've had with Aston Villa and Everton. Same today. All games, again we should be winning and scoring more goals.’

Bompastor: We must be more clinical and find a better balance
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor insists she is happy with the way her Chelsea side are performing, but says they must find a better balance between being solid defensively and creating more goals as they continue to challenge on multiple fronts. The Blues came out 1-0 winners against Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Women’s Champions League in midweek thanks to a late goal from Veerle Buurman. However, they were unable to find another strike to put Liverpool to the sword, despite an incredibly dominant second-half performance. Bompastor says that while her team needs to be more ruthless and clinical, the overall level of play has been impressive. ‘I think right now we need to find a better balance between the defensive aspects,’ Bompastor said in her press conference after the draw against Liverpool. ‘I'm really happy also with the way we build up no matter the opponent; if they come and man-mark, if they leave us a little bit more space. ‘The things we need to improve are in the creation-finishing phase: making sure we create as much as possible in the games and we are clinical and ruthless in the box when we have those opportunities.’ Bompastor said her side have been working on a number of aspects of their attacking play as they look to increase the number of goals scored, but added that sometimes these things do take time to come to fruition. ‘I think we were dominant in the second half,’ she added. ‘We have been working a lot on the final third, in the box, details around the timings of the runs, the positions in the box and the mentality around how we want to attack the box as well. ‘When I talk about being ruthless, clinical, it's the desire to be first on the ball. All these things we have been working on, and we will keep working on. ‘It takes a lot of time sometimes to get those connections right, and to be able to be in the right positions. But we need to keep working because sometimes the difference can be when you start to lose a little bit of confidence in that box, it can change things a little bit. ‘So we need to stay confident and make sure we do everything we can under our control to turn these things around. ‘I'm really happy with a lot of things we are doing right now. When you have ambitions, when you want to win titles, you need to make sure to find the right balance between being strong defensively but also being able to score goals. ‘So yeah, we need to be that team, and I would like to have a better balance in terms of being able to score more.’

news.title: 'We can't let setbacks affect us'

Alonso updates on Caicedo’s game-changing injury
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso feels the injury suffered by Moises Caicedo against Leeds United played a big part in changing the momentum of the game in the visitors’ favour, but knows Chelsea need to respond to those setbacks better in the future. The Blues suffered a 4-1 defeat to Leeds at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon, in our first game since the international break. Caicedo started the game wearing the captain’s armband, but a collision left him in some pain, and eventually brought an early end to his game when the Ecuadorian was replaced by Jordan Henderson in the 22nd minute. ‘It's a knock and we need to wait until tomorrow to see how he is,’ said Alonso, when asked if Caicedo’s injury was serious after the game. ‘He was in pain and let's see how bad it is.’ Although we took the lead shortly after that enforced change, through Emmanuel Emegha’s first Chelsea goal, Leeds responded to level the scores almost immediately and we struggled to recover control of the game after the double setbacks of Caicedo’s injury and Noah Okafor’s goal. ‘What went wrong was after their equaliser, after the change with Moi, we lost completely the momentum,’ continued the Blues manager. ‘Until then we were doing okay. I think that we were creating, playing a lot on the pitch. We were coming out from the pressure, but from that moment, they started believing, we started not believing. ‘After that, we never got the good feeling mentally in any moment and we were not able to come out from the pressure, we didn't get close to their goal, so it completely changed the game.’ Responding to those setbacks is an area our manager knows we need to improve, something he sees as a joint responsibility among himself and his squad. ‘I feel that as a team, as a collective, together we need to support each other,’ Alonso added. ‘Today, together, we need to find solutions to do better because this will happen. ‘On the pitch, they need to go through those moments to say: "Okay, we are still in the game, we still have many minutes to play and the game is not over”. ‘The game still had so many minutes to play and we felt that we didn't recover that good momentum.’

news.title: Bompastor provides Mayra Ramirez and Manaka Matsukubo injury update
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has given an update on Mayra Ramirez and Manaka Matsukubo, with the Chelsea duo eyeing a return from injury. Ramirez missed almost the entire 2025-26 season after undergoing surgery on a hamstring problem, but has been targeting a return to first-team action. After being spotted back with the squad following the win against Paris Saint-Germain in the UEFA Women’s Champions League in midweek, Bompastor was asked how close Ramirez is to making a return for the Blues - but the manager said patience will be key before the striker returns. ‘Yeah, so Mayra is back in the country,’ Bompastor said. ‘I think we are working with her on fitness to make sure she is back with us on the pitch. ‘For now, she is still rehabbing, and she has not been part of the training sessions with the squad. ‘So we need to take the international break also to keep assessing her and see how she evolves, and I will have an update - probably a better update - after the international break. 'But yeah, she missed a lot of the season, the beginning of the season, so she needs time to build up again.' Matsukubo, meanwhile, missed the clash against PSG and was an unused substitute during the Women’s Super League draw against Liverpool. Bompastor said that while the attacker was available to play, she preferred to use other options off the bench following the injury. ‘Yeah, Manaka got a pain in her glute, so we decided to have her in the squad [rather than starting] today,’ Bompastor said. ‘Probably she still wasn't 100 per cent. From what I could observe, I felt other profiles would have been better in this game to come in.’

news.title: Match report: Chelsea 1-4 Leeds
news.body_en: Chelsea succumbed to defeat to Leeds United in the Premier League despite Emmanuel Emegha marking his full debut with his first goal for the club. It was initially the Blues who looked to be the strongest side when we took control of possession midway through the first half, and then the lead when Emegha smashed in the first goal of his Chelsea career left-footed, after good work by Morgan Rogers to tee him up. It was not to last, though, as a couple of minutes later a Leeds long-ball gave them the opportunity to level the scores through Noah Okafor. It remained all square at half-time, but early in the second half the visitors were awarded a penalty when a shot struck Rogers high on the arm, allowing Dominic Calvert-Lewin to take the lead from the spot. Leeds extended their advantage when Okafor got his second of the game from close range after a long-throw was only half cleared and then, as we tried to find a way back into the game, Brendan Aaronson got another for Leeds on the counter late on, sealing Chelsea's fate. Xabi Alonso made four changes to his team, with Emmanuel Emegha leading the attack on his first start for Chelsea, supported by Estevao Willian, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers. Romea Lavia and Moises Caicedo continued in midfield, the latter as captain. Behind them, Josh Acheampong returned to the defence alongside Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana and Pep Chavarria, with Emiliano Martinez back in goal for the Blues. As always when these two old rivals meet, both sets of supporters were making plenty of noise as this game kicked off at Stamford Bridge. On the pitch, it was a slightly cagey opening, as the two teams probed for openings. Emegha set out his stall early on his full Chelsea debut, giving the home fans a taste of what he is all about by mixing it up with the Leeds centre-backs and making his physical presence felt. It was the home side who gradually began to control proceedings, with Acheampong and Estevao in particular linking up well on our right flank at the start. Rogers was trying to find his range from just outside the box with a couple of efforts, but neither keeper had been tested after 15 minutes. However, when Leeds managed to produce their first spell of pressure in the Chelsea half, it almost gave them the opening goal, when Calvert-Lewin got his head on the end of James Justin’s cross, with Martinez relieved to see it come back off the crossbar. Earlier, Caicedo had needed lengthy treatment on his back following a collision in the air, and eventually he was unable to continue, handing the captain’s armband to Colwill as he was replaced by Jordan Henderson midway through the first half. Shortly afterwards, the Blues put that set-back behind us by taking the lead. Rogers got the better of Justin to bring the ball down, surge past Muharemovic in the middle and feed Emegha down the channel. The striker steadied himself and unleashed a venomous left-foot shot to beat Trafford at his near post. It was quite the introduction to the Bridge supporters. Unfortunately, our lead lasted less than three minutes, as Leeds hit straight back. A long ball caused problems as it dropped out of the sky and broke for Okafor in a dangerous position. He carried the ball into the box and was able to divert his finish into the bottom corner to level the scores. The game continued fairly evenly balanced after those two quick goals, but it was Leeds who came closest when Calvert-Lewin flicked a cross wide and headed too close to a grateful Martinez. Muharemovic did get the ball in the net as Leeds' high balls proved dangerous, but it was ruled out for a clear offside, meaning the teams went in for the half-time break level. There was a slightly chaotic start to the second half amidst a series of appeals from both teams, largely ignored by referee Michael Oliver. That was until a shot ricocheted off Rogers in the box five minutes in. Leeds appealed, the penalty was given, and Martinez had no chance as Calvert-Lewin fired into the bottom corner. Rogers tried to hit straight back after we fell behind, but his shot was too close to Trafford to trouble the keeper, and as we attempted to regroup and push back, we fell further behind. It all came from a long throw which was only cleared as far as the edge of the box. Rogers got a foot to Ampadu’s cross but couldn’t prevent it reaching Okafor, who struck into the top corner on the half-volley, from too close for Martinez to react. Alonso turned to his bench in response as Pedro Neto and Danny Welbeck were introduced to our attack, soon followed onto the pitch by Malo Gusto and Geovany Quenda. It seemed to have the desired effect as we regained control of the ball and began to pen Leeds back deep into their own half with 20 minutes remaining, but with a two-goal deficit there was plenty of work to do if Chelsea were to salvage anything from this game. The Blues worked hard for little reward, though. With their lead secured, Leeds dug in stubbornly to prevent us from carving out clear chances. Instead it was the visitors who scored again on the counter, through substitute Brendan Aaronson in added time. news.title: 'Lola Brown is showing a lot of quality'
'We need more belief in front of goal'
Match report: Liverpool 0-0 Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea were held to a draw away at Liverpool in the Women's Super League, with the Blues dominant but unable to force a winner. The result pushed us a further point clear at the top of the table, with Manchester City in action on Sunday afternoon. The Blues were on top early in the first half before Liverpool forced their way into the game before the break. However, after half-time it was all Chelsea as Sonia Bompastor's side went in search of a winner. While the Blues will undoubtedly be frustrated not to come away with all three points, they maintained their unbeaten start to the season. Bompastor made two alterations from the 1-0 UEFA Women’s Champions League win over Paris Saint-Germain, with Lucy Bronze replacing Nathalie Bjorn in defence. Elsewhere, Sjoeke Nusken came in for Aggie Beever-Jones. After a cautious opening 10 minutes, Hannah Hampton was the first goalkeeper called into action. However, it was a fairly tame header that proved an easy stop for our No.1. Moments later came the first real opening for the Blues as Ellie Carpenter raced down the right flank, pushing into the area before looking for Sandy Baltimore with a cut-back. It would have been a certain goal for Baltimore, but the pass was cut out by a Liverpool defender. Keira Walsh then had an effort from just inside the area, but her curled attempt flew wide of the post. The Blues kept the pressure on, with Lexi Potter flashing an effort wide from outside the area. Liverpool's first chance of real note came after 24 minutes, with a blocked clearance allowing Vivien Endemann to get on the ball in the area. However, her lay-off to Natalia Ramos was dragged well wide by the Spanish star. We continued to press forward with Walsh seeing a shot blocked after a short corner, before Alyssa Thompson came close to opening the scoring. The 22-year-old broke forward before firing in a left-footed shot that was pushed over the bar by Khiara Keating. Fuka Nagano then forced a great stop from Hampton. The keeper was alert as the ball dropped to the Liverpool attacker, stopping a fierce effort before gathering the ball at the second attempt. Ramos then came close for the visitors with a free-kick, whipping the ball just over the bar. Both teams went in search of an opener before the break, with Endemann pouncing on a loose pass before firing a shot harmlessly over the bar for the hosts. Ramos then had a shot from outside the box which Hampton did well to parry before collecting. The Blues attacked quickly with five minutes left as Baltimore was found in space down the left, but she couldn't find the back of the net with Keating closing down the angle in the Liverpool goal - as the score remained level at the break. We came out strong to start again, with Carpenter forcing Keating into an intervention from a cross, while Walsh showed quick feet before having a shot blocked. Walsh then forced another save from Keating, her high shot palmed over the bar. From the corner, Veerle Buurman almost poked an effort home but saw her attempt blocked. Bompastor did not leave it long to make a change, with Lola Brown making her way onto the pitch around 10 minutes into the second half, replacing Baltimore. Brown had an instant impact, playing a nice one-two before delivering a cross into the centre, where Thompson just couldn't get over the ball to put her header on target. Carpenter quickly earned another corner for the Blues, flying down the right before firing in a cross which almost deceived Keating. With just over 20 minutes remaining, Brown fired in another dangerous cross; this time Nusken saw a powerful volley pushed behind by the Liverpool keeper. As we entered the final quarter of the contest, Brown fired in another dangerous cross, this time Nusken saw a powerful volley pushed behind by Keating. Walsh then had a snapshot which seemed to take everyone by surprise before rolling just wide. Following a scramble in the area, Broze did well to find Walsh again on the right side of the area, but her shot was again well-saved by Keating. Potter then had an opportunity, attempting to place an effort past Keating but seeing her shot stopped. Bompastor made one last throw of the dice in the final 10 minutes as Beever-Jones, Erin Cuthbert and Giulia Dragoni were introduced, with Thompson, Kaptein and Nusken making way. A stop-start finish to the game ensued, with the Blues unable to create any more clear-cut chances before referee Ben Speedie blew up for full-time. We remain unbeaten and go two points clear at the top of the Women’s Super League, but will head into the international break in second place if Manchester City beat Tottenham on Sunday. This was the last fixture before the final international break of the year. That means we are not back in action until Saturday 12 December, when we take on London City Lionesses at Stamford Bridge in the Women's Super League. And you can secure your spot by clicking here. news.title: Xabi Alonso on Emmanuel Emegha selection for Leeds clash
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes Emmanuel Emegha is ready to take his opportunity against Leeds United, as the Dutch forward prepares to make his first start for the Blues. Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge following the two-week international break, with Alonso determined to see his side get back to winning ways against Leeds. The forward made his Blues debut in our Carabao Cup clash against Liverpool and earned his first Premier League minutes against Sunderland before the international break, and now Alonso has included him from the off for the first time this afternoon. Explaining his selection, Alonso said: 'We have seen a lot from him, but he needed to build his fitness because he had picked up a few injuries. Now he's been training for a long time, he's played some minutes, he's been patiently working hard and now he's got the chance to start. 'And today, hopefully, he has a good game and he's feeling good.' With Emegha joined in attack by Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Estevao Willian, Alonso is hoping to see plenty of creativity from his side. However, the Blues manager has stressed that maintaining the right balance between attack and defence will be crucial against Leeds. The boss continued: 'Our attacking players need to be ready to defend, ready to have this solidity that is needed in these kind of games. 'But as well, we need creativity, we need to be a threat in the last third. With these players we can have it, but we need to play a complete game.'

news.title: U18 Premier League Full Match: Chelsea U18s vs Arsenal U18s
U18 Premier League Highlights: Chelsea U18s vs Arsenal U18s
Under-18 Premier League report: Chelsea 5-0 Arsenal
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s put on a five-star performance against rivals Arsenal to move us three points clear at the top of the Under-18 Premier League table. Reggie Watson set the tone inside seven minutes, tucking in a rebound from a penalty, before Chizaram Ezenwata got in on the action 11 minutes later. The tempo was unmanageable for Arsenal, who couldn’t handle our ruthless front line. Before the break, Ezenwata had his second goal of the afternoon, tapping in after Riley Ebho’s shot on goal was parried out. After the interval, it was more of the same from Dan Hogan’s side. Mathis Eboue made it four with a well-struck shot into the top corner, before Watson topped the performance with the goal of the match. His free-kick from 30 yards out earned a standing ovation from the crowd at Cobham as Chelsea claimed all three points in a very one-sided derby day. Our Young Blues took the game to Arsenal immediately, and the visitors struggled to handle the pressure. As early as the seventh minute, the pace proved too much. Eboue won a penalty on his return to the side, beating Arsenal goalkeeper Charlie Phillips to a loose ball after Ebho’s shot on goal was turned away. Watson stepped up and went across his body, aiming for the left corner, his spot kick was saved but came straight back out to him, allowing the Englishman to tap home. It didn’t take long until we made it two, as Grimwade retrieved the ball out on the right wing. He played a speculative through ball into the path of Ezenwata, who had some running to do. The Blues forward was in a foot race with Phillips and got to the ball just in time to nudge it around the goalkeeper before slotting it into an empty net. Showing our dominance, it took until the 28th minute for Arsenal to register a shot on target, which Freddy Bernal saved superbly with his right leg. Ebho’s overlapping runs posed huge problems for Arsenal’s defence, just after the half-hour mark, his presence led to our third of the afternoon. Ebho’s strike across goal was denied but straight into the path of Ezenwata, who tapped in his second goal. We maintained the same tempo in the second half, as Eboue came close to our fourth. He cut inside and let fly, only to be denied by a small deflection. From the subsequent corner, Yisa Alao’s half-volley zipped past Dante Waite, who couldn’t quite reach the ball to turn it goalward. Minutes into the second half, we conceded a penalty, as the referee deemed Alao to have brought Abraham Owusu-Gyasi down. Emerson Nwaneri stepped up to take the spot kick and aimed for the left corner, but Bernal read the situation well and made a top save before claiming the rebound. In additional time, he was forced to make another incredible stop, keeping our clean sheet intact. Eboue deservedly got his goal in the end, and what a strike it was. Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli played the ball into Eboue’s path and the Blues winger struck it true into the top right corner. With 20 minutes left on the clock, Ezenwata came inches away from a hat-trick. His chance arose when Isaac Badu whipped in a superb cross towards the six-yard box – Ezenwata met the cross and headed towards the far corner, but his effort skewed just wide. It was the 18-year-old’s final contribution of the match, as moments later he was replaced by Kwamina Ampah. Watson provided the cherry on top in the 87th minute with a spectacular free kick from long range. The 16-year-old curled the ball right into the top corner, taking a nick off the crossbar on the way. It was an incredible strike to complete Watson’s brace and a fantastic way to cap a statement victory. Our emphatic win over Arsenal keeps us top of the Under-18 Premier League on 24 points, three points clear of second place after 11 matches. We are on the road next time out, as we make the short trip to south London to play Crystal Palace. That match is on Saturday 28 November at 11am and will be shown on CFC+. news.title: Alonso underlines importance of control on and off the ball
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has highlighted Chelsea’s ability to control the game, both when in and out of possession, as key to our chances of victory against Leeds United, as well as the games which follow. The Blues host Leeds at Stamford Bridge at 3pm this afternoon, as we return to Premier League action following the last international break of the year. Giving his thoughts on today’s game and what his team needs to do to secure all three points, one aspect was clearly high in his mind, underlining a key aspect he has been working on with his players at Cobham. ‘We have had spells with control, other spells that I would like us to have better control,’ Alonso explained. ‘I'm not meaning just control with the ball. Sometimes you can have control without the ball because things are going the way you have planned. You feel comfortable that “okay we don't have the ball, but we know what we are doing”. ‘When you have an idea where you feel comfortable that the opponent has the ball and where you don't feel comfortable that the opponent has the ball, and when you know that they have the ball where you want them to have it, you can feel good control of the game. ‘It's something that's in my mind, because that's the way I like to play, but we are working for that to get better.’ Control could also be particularly important against a Leeds side who seems to relish the physical aspects of the game and exploiting the loose-ball situations that result from them. No team in the Premier League has won as many individual duels as the Whites this season. However, Alonso is reluctant to view that as a purely physical or mental challenge. He sees everything in football as being linked, with the issue of control again at the forefront, but admits it is an obstacle his players will need to overcome. ‘First of all, it's the Premier League. It's not just against Leeds, that will happen next week against Forest, and the next one against Palace. This is the level of the competition and we know how important it can be,’ said our manager. ‘It's not just the duels. It's about the football things or the tactical things. When you have good control, normally you are in better positions to face duels. When you don't have that much control, you are not in that good position. ‘So it's not just about going one-v-one and let's see what happens. No, I think that you can help situations, to be stronger in the duels. After, for sure, it's the individual qualities that help a lot, but you can help as well. ‘It's also tactical things. Because for me, everything comes with, for sure, the mentality, but many things are down to the football reasons. When we analyse we can talk about lacking intensity, but why did we lack intensity? Why didn't we press well? Why were the distances there? What did we or didn't we do in the trigger moments or trying to squeeze? ‘So mainly I focus on the football things because I think that if that works, in the mental things it helps the players.’ The Blues will no doubt be tested physically and mentally when we return to the pitch in the highly competitive surroundings of the Premier League this afternoon, but Alonso seems confident his team can pass with flying colours.

news.title: Opposition scout – Leeds United
news.body_en: Ahead of Chelsea's Premier League meeting with Leeds United, we take a closer look at the Whites, their approach under Daniel Farke and the players who could make an impact. This fixture was played out at Stamford Bridge as recently as late September – a 6-3 Carabao Cup victory for Chelsea – though both teams were much-changed for the floodlit competition. Daniel Farke set his team up in a 3-4-3 formation against Xabi Alonso’s 4-3-3 and may repeat the formation on Saturday. Before the break at Elland Road, two of his substitutes combined to notch the only goal of the game against Tottenham – Harry Wilson feeding striker Noah Okafor. That was the former Switzerland international’s second of the campaign – each of leading marksman Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s three league goals this term has come at home too. Critics suggest they are underscoring in the league: they have the joint fewest away goals in the Premier League – three. That said, England keeper James Trafford has the highest saves-per-shot rate in the top flight – 81.7 per cent. They also boast the third-meanest defence in the division, with Slovenia international Tarik Muharemovic proving a smart signing – and one of six ever-presents in the league. A potentially decisive battleground is set plays. Farke’s men have generated the most xG from set pieces (6.1, excluding penalties) – their two goals in the past four league games came from a throw-in and a corner. Farke will be without Mateo Joseph, though Anton Stach could return.

news.title: Chelsea vs Leeds Utd | Primed for battle at the Bridge
Bompastor highlights Cuthbert's importance ahead of 'difficult' Liverpool test
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has underlined Erin Cuthbert’s importance to Chelsea as the club captain targets a return to the starting XI for our Women’s Super League clash against Liverpool. Cuthbert has appeared as a substitute in our last three games, and Bompastor stated that a knock suffered in the draw against Hacken prevented her from starting the win against title rivals Manchester City. The Blues coach added that Cuthbert is now back fit enough to be competing for a starting role, but admitted that the competition for places is currently fierce because of the performances from her team-mates. ‘I always talk to my players and give them the reality in terms of where they are in terms of the performances,’ Bompastor said. ‘So when we started this block we had a really good conversation with Erin saying to her what our ambitions for the block were and the plan. ‘I think probably when she got that knock against Hacken at the end of the game, she made a little step back and the plan was for her to be able to start the Man City game but she couldn't - I think she was not 100 per cent for that game. ‘After the scenario of the game when the substitutions didn't help, right now she's not far from starting games. I think she's fit enough to be able do that, but the team is performing at a really good level. ‘I'm also really happy with the performances from the other players who are playing right now. So she knows what she needs to do and she's an important player for us. ‘Going into the game we will need to bring some energy, some fresh legs; she didn't play much [against PSG] so she will be probably fresh and ready to start if she has to.’ Asked whether her team might need the ‘bite’ that Cuthbert brings for the battle against Liverpool, Bompastor admitted that she hadn’t yet made a decision on her starters for Saturday - but highlighted the midfielder’s importance to the team and the different aspects she could bring to some team-mates. '[It could be] a good game for her to play. Again, she's a really important player for us,’ Bompastor said. ‘She's our captain, she brings a lot of quality. ‘When she's on the pitch, she's a different profile from some of the players who are playing right now. I will analyse Liverpool again and see what is the most appropriate for us to start the game with and maybe bringing also an impact from the bench.’

news.title: Chelsea vs Leeds: All you need to know
news.body_en: An age-old, long-distance rivalry is rekindled at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton preview the 99th instalment of northern grit versus King’s Road swagger at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea host Leeds United just ten weeks after the Yorkshiremen’s recent cup visit. The Blues delivered a thrilling 6-3 victory over the Whites in that Carabao Cup encounter and the visitors have not won at the Bridge on any front for more than a quarter of a century. However, before the international break, Leeds beat Tottenham Hotspur 1-0 for their first three-point haul since September. They stand ninth in the table, while the Londoners slipped to fifth after defeat at Sunderland by the same score. Xabi Alonso’s side also rank fifth for points gained on home soil this season, while Daniel Farke’s men are 11th-best on the road. Last season, this fixture finished 2-2, the Blues having led 2-0 until well past the hour mark. We also won 1-0 in the FA Cup to make it ten unbeaten against the Yorkshiremen. Chelsea are already eight points better off than in the corresponding ten fixtures last season and could return to fourth place with a win. The good news from Alonso’s pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon was that Josh Acheampong, Moises Caicedo and Emiliano Martinez are all available to feature against Leeds following the international break. ‘Moises is ready to start,’ our manager confirmed. ‘It was discussed after playing the first game [for Ecuador] he could save some minutes. That was good for him, and he’s fine.’ ‘Emi is in the squad and he is selectable. Against Sunderland two weeks ago probably there was risk, and the plan was for him to train more with Argentina and to play one game. It went well so he’s available.’ However, Jamie Gittens, Jorrel Hato, Reece James, Joao Pedro and Maxence Lacroix all remain out of contention as they continue to work on their recovery at Cobham. ‘Joao’s not yet fit to train with the team. We need to wait a bit more. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see day-by-day how he is feeling. ‘Jorrel has a back problem. We need to be patient because it’s going to take a while.’ Though they were played on neutral soil, the epic 1970 final battles between Chelsea and Leeds, in pursuit of an FA Cup neither ha won at the time, are always mentioned in regard to this fixture. For those who witnessed the 2-2 at Wembley and the Blues’ stunning victory thanks to David Webb’s header at Old Trafford, the intrigue, culture clash, violence and satisfying conclusion were unforgettable. They established the tone for relations between the two camps for generations. The Whites most recently returned to the top flight in 2025 and the Blues had won every visit during their previous three-season tenancy between 2020 and 2023. In the Covid-restricted meeting in December 2020, attended by 2,000 at the Bridge, Cobham graduate Patrick Bamford broke the deadlock, but Marco Bielsa’s side saw Oliver Giroud restore parity, then Kurt Zouma and Christian Pulisic deliver a 3-1win. History repeated itself the following year, with Leeds edging ahead through a penalty, before Mason Mount levelled. After the interval, Jorginho put the European champions ahead, also from 12 yards. The Yorkshiremen equalised with seven minutes remaining, but at the death a rare second spot-kick conversion by Jorginho settled the game at 3-2. Wesley Fofana’s first league goal for Chelsea was enough to claim the points in March 2023, a few months before Javi Gracia’s side were relegated. Last February, Leeds came back from goals by Joao Pedro and Cole Palmer to draw 2-2, scoring with their only shots on target. Chelsea’s tally of 13 Premier League goals on home soil has been bettered only by Brighton (15). The Blues have recorded the highest shot accuracy in the top flight this season – 41.9 per cent. Between the international breaks, the Blues conceded one goal from open play, two from corners and two penalties. Nottingham Forest (nine) and Sunderland (eight) are the only top-flight clubs to have scored fewer goals so far than Leeds (ten). The Whites have opened the scoring in three of their five away league matches. Mike Penders, honoured for last month’s finger-tip save against Man Utd, is Chelsea’s first recipient of the Premier League Save of the Month award since Robert Sanchez in October 2024, and our fourth ever. news.title: Latest update on James and Lacroix returns from Alonso
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso discussed the chances of Reece James and Maxence Lacroix getting back on the pitch before the end of the year, as the pair continue their recovery from injury. Both players have been absent in recent weeks - our captain James after undergoing minor knee surgery, centre-back Lacroix due to a hamstring issue. The duo are working hard to get back in the action with Chelsea as soon as possible, but Alonso had already confirmed that our next fixture against Leeds United on Saturday will be too soon for either of them to be involved. The Spaniard has now provided further clarity around hopes that James and Lacroix could be back out on the pitch for the Blues before the end of 2026. ‘I think that Max has a better chance than Reece,’ our manager revealed. ‘It’s not definitely that Reece won’t be back before then, but Max has a better chance.’ James and Lacroix have been important figures in Alonso’s team, starting all but one of the Premier League matches they have been available for. Just like Joao Pedro and Moises Caicedo, who have missed games in recent weeks, their absence would be a blow for any team. However, the Chelsea manager knows that injuries are an unavoidable part of football, and insists it is up to him and the other players to be ready to find solutions on the pitch. ‘We want to have a complete squad, for sure. That's the goal of any manager,’ added Alonso. ‘We have built a good squad, knowing that some players, they have this experience, they have this role, they have this specificity that is very needed, and we are a better team with them. ‘But it's not about making a big drama when someone gets injured, because that happens. So we need to deal with that. ‘We need to find the other players that are available. They need to show that they are good enough, and that's our dynamic.’ Those selected in Alonso’s next starting line-up will be looking to do just that when we host Leeds United at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League for a 3pm kick-off on Saturday. news.title: Penders reflects on PL Save of the Month
Alonso says Blues are ‘building an identity’ but need consistency
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes his Chelsea side are well on their way to forming the ‘identity’ he wants to see from them, even though he knows it is a process that takes time. Alonso arrived this summer, since when the Blues have had some standout results, such as the thrilling home wins over Brighton and Bournemouth. The manager recognises the next step is consistency. Developing the character of the team in order to be competitive on a regular basis is his aim. ‘We are building it,’ Alonso said on his team’s identity. ‘I think that this is a process. ‘The goal for us is that we feel that this is our idea of how we want to play, knowing the context, knowing the Premier League, but that we are prepared with whoever we are facing, and that we are competitive. ‘We want to be competitive, and that's the goal. We are lacking a bit of consistency on the results for sure. We have won some games, but had some defeats as well, and we are in that process to get better. It will take a while.’ Leeds provide stiff opposition in our first game back after the international break. Alonso is acutely aware of how tough they are to play against both physically and tactically. They have conceded just eight goals in ten games, and have only been beaten twice. ‘We know that nowadays you need to be flexible each game, even during the game, that one structure can change with the ball, without the ball,’ Alonso said. ‘Leeds are a demanding team, not just physically, tactically as well. They are doing great things with the manager they have. They have been together, so they have a pretty clear idea, and it's going to be a very demanding game.' Alonso added exactly what he wants from his players as they look to get back to winning ways at Stamford Bridge. ‘We need to work,' he said. 'We need to be patient. We need to be intense. We need to have a good concentration and focus, and to know that each detail can be very important.’ There's still time to secure your place for Chelsea v Leeds at Stamford Bridge. news.title: Cobham Unseen: pre-Leeds Utd (h)
Training gallery: Blues make last preparations for Leeds
Alonso: Emegha and Welbeck ready to offer Blues alternative
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso says Emmanuel Emegha and Danny Welbeck are both ready to play their part against Leeds in the absence of Joao Pedro in attack. The Brazilian striker has missed the last four games through injury, and Alonso confirmed that Chelsea’s No.9 would not be back in time for this weekend’s Premier League clash, our first since the final international break of 2026. Emegha and Welbeck both arrived at Stamford Bridge this summer, and have largely featured from the bench so far. Alonso says both are capable of stepping into the fold in attack, and can offer different strengths as alternatives in Joao Pedro’s absence. ‘They are both ready,’ Alonso said at his press conference on Friday afternoon. ‘Both different qualities, different stages of a career. Danny has played so many games, he has great experience, he has quality. And Eme, he has this power, this physicality. He's waiting for the chance, and we have enough games to try. ‘It's not just the strikers who can score,’ added Alonso. ‘We need the whole team for that. We can score in set-pieces from defenders, midfielders. So it's teamwork, for sure. ‘Joao is an important player, but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options, and we need to keep trying.’ Alonso also praised Mike Penders for the way he adapted to replacing Emiliano Martinez in goal. The young Belgian started games after Martinez suffered a nasty jaw injury away at Everton in October. Following an individual error in the defeat to Tottenham, Alonso was pleased to see the 21-year-old’s reaction, commending him for the progress he has made in a short space of time. ‘Mike has done very good things,’ Alonso said. ‘I think that we know the progression that he had, that he overcame a difficult moment for sure after the first game. But after he's done better. ‘He's improving, and with his minutes, his development has been good.’

news.title: Club statement
news.body_en: Chelsea FC can confirm the club has been fined by The Football Association following a charge of misconduct in relation to the FA Cup away fixture at Charlton Athletic on Saturday 10 January 2026. An independent Regulatory Commission has imposed a £150,000 fine, an action plan and a warning regarding the future conduct of supporters following abusive, offensive and discriminatory chanting. We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club. Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this. Chelsea takes a zero-tolerance approach towards discriminatory behaviour in whatever form it takes. We will always take steps to identify those responsible and take appropriate action where necessary. Discriminatory behaviour may constitute a criminal offence and supporters found to have breached the club’s regulations will face disciplinary action, including possible match bans or membership suspensions. We will also require all those who may be sanctioned to take part in the Kick it Out programme as we believe education is as important as sanctions in order to root out this behaviour for good. We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward. news.title: Alonso Press Conference 🎙️
Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Leeds
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has provided an update on the fitness of several members of his Chelsea squad, including Joao Pedro, Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix, Moises Caicedo, Emiliano Martinez and Jorrel Hato. He also reported the latest on longer-term absentees Reece James and Jamie Gittens. The Blues are back in action this weekend following the final international break of 2026. We host Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, hoping to return to winning ways after losing at Sunderland last time out. Alonso confirmed he will not be able to call upon the services of Joao Pedro, who hasn’t played since the win at Everton last month because of a thigh issue. ‘He’s not yet fit to train with the team,’ said Alonso. ‘We need to wait a bit more. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see day by day how he is feeling.’ Alonso said Lacroix, who has a hamstring problem, is in a ‘similar situation’ to the Brazilian striker and will not be able to feature against Leeds. The manager also ruled Hato out. He said: ‘Jorrel has a back problem. We need to be patient because it’s going to take a while.’ There was better news regarding Acheampong and Caicedo. Acheampong didn’t play for England Under-21s during the international break, while Caicedo came off at half-time in Ecuador’s most recent friendly. ‘Moises is ready to start. It was discussed after playing the first game he could save some minutes. That was good for him, and he’s fine.’ Alonso replied with an affirmative ‘yes’ when asked if Acheampong can return to action, while he also provided an update on Martinez, who represented his country during the international break. ‘He is in the squad and he is selectable,’ said Alonso. ‘Against Sunderland two weeks ago probably there was risk, and the plan was for him to train more with Argentina and to play one game. It went well so he’s available for tomorrow.’ Alonso’s final fitness news regarded James and Gittens, who have not played for us since September. ‘Reece is getting there. He’s taking a step forward, but still needs some weeks. ‘Jamie Gittens is better,’ added Alonso. ‘He’s already training with the team, but we want to give him more time until he comes back in the squad.’ There's still time to secure your place for Chelsea v Leeds at Stamford Bridge. news.title: Made in Cobham: Andrew Pennie
news.body_en: From a football-mad childhood to growing up at Chelsea, Andrew Pennie reflects on the people, experiences and lessons that have shaped him on and off the pitch, fresh from signing his first professional contract with the Blues. For most of Andrew Pennie's life, football and Chelsea have been constants – and both have shaped the player and person he is today. Growing up in Lewisham with two older brothers, there was rarely a quiet moment in the Pennie house. Our young forward remembers playing EA FC [then known as FIFA] with his siblings and naturally claims he was the best. The rivalry occasionally got the better of him, but it was all part of growing up in a household where football was never far away. ‘It was chaotic,' he says with a smile. 'We would make too much noise in the house, but it was good.' It was Pennie's brothers who sparked his interest in football, and his first memory of kicking a ball around is as a four-year-old in a concrete courtyard outside his home. While not the most storied introduction to the beautiful game, it was the start of a journey that has shaped many chapters of Pennie’s life. It started at grassroots level, with Pennie playing Sunday League football for All Stars United. He was identified by Chelsea’s recruitment team and joined our development centre. Yet there were also sessions undertaken with Arsenal. However, the Blues proved the right fit and Pennie signed as an Under-9 with Chelsea. He says: ‘At the development centre I didn’t feel nervous – I was happy because going pro was always the ambition. I wanted to be a policeman when I was three but other than that it was always football.’ His family was delighted with the decision, and many attended his signing day at Stamford Bridge. ‘I think there were 15 people there on the day!' he recalls. 'I probably didn’t realise how big of a deal it was at the time. ‘If I could go back now and give my eight-year-old self some advice, I’d have told him to always look at the positives because there are ups and downs. I don’t like to focus on the downs.’ In the years since, Pennie has enjoyed plenty of high moments. A standout season was his Under-14 year, when he felt his performances were particularly strong and his belief in having a future in football grew. Pennie's favourite memory, though, remains winning the Under-12 Truce Cup in 2021. He scored three goals in five matches despite not yet having moved into an attacking role. 'I was a centre-back when I was younger, then a right-back aged 12,' he says. 'I wasn’t a forward until I was 13 years old. During one training session before a game against Southampton, I played up front and couldn’t stop scoring. ‘I found out I might be playing as a striker, but I didn’t want to because I was too nervous. Kwamina Ampah was pushing me and I think he said something to the coaches. I started up front against Southampton that weekend and we won 5-1. I scored four and ever since I’ve been a forward.’ Having moved into digs close to our training ground at 14 years old, Cobham has become Pennie’s home. Much of his development has come within the club’s environment and he believes Chelsea has ‘shaped me a lot as a person and how I view the world.' There have been challenges, but Pennie used each as motivation to keep getting better. After one particularly tough match, he received the advice to ‘train how I want to play’. The message stuck and Pennie now identifies his ‘bounce back’ mentality as one of the biggest improvements in his game. His family’s influence has extended well beyond those early footballing memories. Growing up, Pennie’s mother would make the hour-and-15-minute journey from home in Lewisham to Cobham every day. That commitment has never been taken for granted. 'My parents are my heroes; they are always in a positive mood and often pray for me,' he says. 'I know they are very proud of me.’ Away from the pitch, he describes himself as peaceful, although the competitive streak developed over games of FIFA and football with his brothers remains. He now often plays padel with his Chelsea team-mates and previously enjoyed basketball and cricket before focusing on football. His ambitions continue to grow in a blue shirt. Pennie wants to improve his movement off the ball and is chasing down a personal goal target for the season. Pennie's journey has been underpinned by hard work and shaped by tough lessons. He has experienced the highs of winning and finding his place on the pitch, alongside the natural challenges and disappointments that come with life as a young player. Still just 17 years old, much more is to be written in Pennie's story. With good people around him and our Academy as a nurturing backdrop, he will not lack for inspiration in the years ahead.
